newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians bury student killed in clash.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians bury student killed in clash.

text.p: Chanting "with blood and spirit we sacrifice ourselves for Palestine", hundreds of mourners on Sunday buried a 20-year-old Arab student shot dead by Israeli soldiers in a West Bank clash.

Abdullah Khalil Salah, a resident of Beit Sahour in the West Bank near Bethlehem, on Saturday became the first Palestinian killed in 10 days of violence over Israel's construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Church bells pealed on Easter Sunday and Koran verses were broadcast over loudspeakers while Palestinians carried Salah's body -- wrapped in a red, white, green and black Palestinian flag -- on a stretcher from his house to a mosque for burial.
A Palestinian police jeep covered with flowers and wreaths led a procession of some 1,000 people who took part in the funeral.
Some carried placards which read: "No peace with settlement" and "Yes to peace, no to giving up".
A Palestinian policeman bid farewell to the dead man by firing several shots from his rifle into the air.

Similar demonstrations took place in other West Bank and Gaza Strip areas under Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's rule on Land Day, an annual day of protest against Israel's confiscation of Arab lands.

Israeli soldiers fired rubber bullets and teargas at hundreds of Palestinians who broke through Palestinian police lines to charge a Jewish settlement near the self-ruled West Bank town of Jenin, witnesses said.

In the West Bank town of Hebron, protesters carried signs which read "No peace without the release of Palestinian prisoners", "No peace with settlements", and "Hebron is an Islamic city. The occupation must go".

In Gaza City, some 500 dignitaries from all shades of the Palestinian political spectrum took part in a protest march carrying signs that read: "No peace with settlements" and "Settlements are terrorism".

Palestinians were enraged when Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on the settlement last week on a hilltop they call Jabal Abu Ghneim and Israelis call Har Homa. Washington vetoed two U.N. Security Council resolutions against the settlement.

In references to Netanyahu and U.S. President Bill Clinton, Gazan marchers chanted: "Netanyahu, Netanyahu, patience, patience, Abu Ghneim will be your grave" and "Clinton coward, Clinton coward, the veto is the biggest proof".

Netanyahu called on Israeli Arabs to shun violence on Land Day, which also commemorates the 1976 killing by Israeli security forces of six Arabs protesting against expropriation of land by the government.
Witnesses saw about 20 tanks parked at an Israeli military camp south of the West Bank town of Nablus -- up from 12 the previous day.
The Israeli army and paramilitary border police, aided by tanks and helicopters, had already beefed up their West Bank forces.
